caption:
An AI built a seat map for a booking page. Book one seat and every row shows it.

Look at the card. fill([]) creates one empty array and puts that same array in all three slots. rows[0], rows[1] and rows[2] all point to it, so a push through any of them shows up in all of them.

Array.from({ length: 3 }, () => []) calls the function once per slot, so each row gets its own array.

The same trap applies to fill({}) with objects. fill(0) or fill('') is fine, because numbers and strings aren't shared references.

Source: MDN, Array.prototype.fill() (filling with an object).
